wine-quality.why: A prediction task on a dataset with no traps at all: eleven clean numeric measurements and a score. The point is what the systems do when nothing is hidden.
wine-quality.what_happened: Both reached for a random forest and both landed just under the threshold: better than a linear regression (0.575) and short of the reference forest (0.424). Neither tuned anything, and neither compared its model with a simpler one.
wine-quality.baselines: always predicting the mean gives MAE 0.658, a linear regression 0.575, a random forest 0.424

student-grades.why: An analytical task on a small file that is semicolon-separated with quoted text, where the interesting part is reading the file correctly and grouping by two coded columns.
student-grades.what_happened: Both parsed the file and matched all nine numbers. The baseline did it in a single model call.

household-power.why: The hardest of the three for a machine: 2,075,259 rows, readings written as `?`, dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and a question about one month inside four years of minutes.
household-power.what_happened: Both read the file with `na_values='?'` and an explicit `format='%d/%m/%Y'`, so neither lost a day to a misparsed date, and both matched the count of missing minutes, all 31 daily means and the peak day. It is worth putting next to T11, where runs died on the 4 GB sandbox limit: the limit is not a problem for two million rows read sensibly, it was a problem for a dense one-hot matrix of a hundred thousand.

conclusions: **On unseen data with a clear goal, both systems work.** Six runs, six right answers, including a two-million-row file and a model that had to beat a linear regression.

**The team's machinery bought nothing here.** Same answers as the single model, for 4 to 9 times the model calls and 2 to 3 times the wall clock. That is the same finding as `docs/ablations.md`, on data neither system was tuned for.
**This is why the benchmark has traps.** These three tasks have no planted pitfalls, and everything passed. The differences between systems only appear where a dataset punishes a plausible mistake.
